LanguageData.CC_Match_Menu_Title: Whom to match with {OTHER}, and where they would live
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_DiplomacyMarriage: Matches between the colony's people and theirs, the wedding with their kin, and the alliance that follows.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_DiplomacyMarriage_Tip: A match between one of the colony's and one of a people at peace: "Speak for a match" face to face with one of theirs at the colony (two lovers speak for themselves), a letter to their notable (the people's card lists who would fit), or their own offer, once a year at most when their head thinks 40 or more of the colony. Who may marry is the game's own rule: grown, drawn to each other, not kin, free to take a spouse by their faith, and the Empire's titled nobles only to a titled colonist. The colonist is asked first: a match they are against comes before the council with their objection. Where the couple lives is chosen each time: theirs comes to live at the colony with their kin as the wedding's guests, or the colonist goes to live at their town for good. While the marriage holds, their notables think 15 better of the colony, their kin send a gift each season, they write when a raiders' camp is set against the colony, and it stands as a defense pact (never with the Empire); a child of the two keeps it after a death. A spouse wronged by the colony (killed, imprisoned, enslaved, sold or banished) is the gravest wrong their people remember, with a grudge that passes from head to head. Off: nothing new is matched or offered, a match agreed goes ahead, and a marriage holds.

LanguageData.CC_Match_Ans_Moot: {PEOPLE} can't take it up as things stand. {WHY}

LanguageData.CC_Match_Ans_NoNever: {PEOPLE} don't think well enough of the colony to give one of theirs to it, and said no to {WORD} with {OURS} without weighing it.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Ans_Yes: {PEOPLE} have agreed to {WORD}: {OURS} and {THEIRS} are promised to each other, to be married by {RITE}. {LIVES}.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Ans_ButAgainst: {OURS} is against it, and the council will hear {OURS_objective} out before anything is settled.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Agreed_Colony: {OURS} and {THEIRS} of {PEOPLE} are promised to each other: {WORD}, by {RITE}. On the day, {THEIRS} walks in from {TOWN} with {THEIRS_possessive} kin as the wedding's guests, joins the colony at the gate, and is married to {OURS} here. The guests stay for the evening's feast and go home at first light.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Agreed_Theirs: {OURS} and {THEIRS} of {PEOPLE} are promised to each other: {WORD}, by {RITE}. On the day, {THEIRS} and one of {THEIRS_possessive} kin come to the gate for {OURS}, who walks out to them and goes to live at {TOWN} for good. The wedding is held there, and their letter will tell of it.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Agreed_Risks: While the marriage holds, {PEOPLE} think better of the colony, answer its call as a defense pact does and call on it in turn, and their kin send a gift each season. A spouse from among them wronged by the colony (killed, imprisoned, enslaved, sold or banished) is the gravest wrong {PEOPLE} remember, and their head would hold a grudge that passes to the next.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Agreed_Pressed: The council pressed it over the objection {OURS} made, and {OURS} will not forget it soon.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Gifts: Gifts go both ways at the gate, by their ways: porters of {PEOPLE} bring {THEIRS}, and carry the colony's gift of {OURS} home with them.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Gifts_NoneOurs: Porters of {PEOPLE} bring their gift, {THEIRS}, to the gate. The colony has no silver to give in return, and {PEOPLE} noticed.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Offer: {WHO} of {PEOPLE} writes to offer {WORD}: {THEIRS} for {OURS}, married by {RITE}.
LanguageData.CC_Match_What: If it is agreed, gifts go both ways at the gate, and on the day the couple's kin come. While the marriage holds, {PEOPLE} think better of the colony, answer its call as a defense pact does and call on it in turn, and send a small gift each season. A spouse wronged by the colony is the gravest wrong they remember. A colonist against the match is heard by the council before anything is settled.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Opt_AcceptAsk: Agree, and let the council hear {OURS}
LanguageData.CC_Match_Msg_Moot: The match {PEOPLE} offered can't go ahead now. {WHY}
LanguageData.CC_Impact_MatchPress: {OURS} is promised to {THEIRS} all the same, and it weighs on {OURS} for a long while.
LanguageData.CC_Impact_MatchWithdraw: Word goes to {PEOPLE} that the match is off, and they feel turned down.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Arrive: {THEIRS} of {PEOPLE} has walked in with {THEIRS_possessive} kin and joined the colony at the gate. The two will be married today, before the evening, if nothing gets in the way; the guests will watch, and sit at the colony's table tonight. At home, {PEOPLE} would hold it by {RITE}.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Arrive_Alone: {THEIRS} of {PEOPLE} has walked in alone and joined the colony. {THEIRS} and {OURS} will be married here by the colony's own ceremony, on a quiet day.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Escort_Comes: {THEIRS} and one of {PEOPLE} have come from {TOWN} for {OURS}, and are walking up to the gate.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Leaves: {OURS} walked out to {THEIRS} at the gate, said {OURS_possessive} goodbyes, and left with them for {TOWN}. {OURS} is one of {PEOPLE} now, and will be married there.
LanguageData.CC_Match_HereAs_Kin: come for {OURS}, kin of the one {OURS} marries
LanguageData.CC_Match_Wed: {OURS} and {THEIRS} are married, here at the colony, with kin of {THEIRS} from {TOWN} among the guests. It is {WORD} now, and {PEOPLE} count the colony as family.
LanguageData.CC_Match_WedAway: Word has come from {TOWN}: {OURS} and {THEIRS} were married there, by {RITE}. {OURS} lives among {PEOPLE} now, and they count the colony as family.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Wed_What: While it holds, the notables of {PEOPLE} think {REGARD} better of the colony, their kin send a small gift each season, and they write when trouble is coming. It stands as a defense pact between the two: their fighters come when the colony calls, and they will call on the colony's in turn.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Wed_WhatPactHad: While it holds, the notables of {PEOPLE} think {REGARD} better of the colony, their kin send a small gift each season, and they write when trouble is coming. The colony's defense pact with them runs on for as long as the marriage holds.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Wed_WhatEmpire: While it holds, the notables of {PEOPLE} think {REGARD} better of the colony, their kin send a small gift each season, and they write when trouble is coming. The Empire makes no pacts, and this marriage is no pact either.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Wed_NoRoom: The colony already has three marriages with {PEOPLE}: this one is the couple's own, and adds nothing more between the two peoples.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Hist_WedAway: {OURS} married {THEIRS} at {TOWN} and went to live among {PEOPLE}.
LanguageData.CC_Match_PactAgain: The marriage with {PEOPLE} stands as a defense pact again, a year after the last one closed.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Off_Died: The match between {OURS} and {THEIRS} has come to nothing: {NAME} is dead.

LanguageData.CC_Match_Off_KinGone: The kin of {PEOPLE} who came for {OURS} are gone, and the match is off.

LanguageData.CC_Match_Off_ByColony: The colony has called off the match between {OURS} and {THEIRS}. {PEOPLE} take it as the colony's word broken.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Off_Wronged: {NAME}, promised to one of the colony's, was {WRONG}. {PEOPLE} will not forget it.

LanguageData.CC_Match_Wrong_Enslaved: made a slave of the colony

LanguageData.CC_Match_KinGift_Away: {OURS} and {THEIRS} sent {GIFT} from {TOWN} for the season, carried in by a courier of {PEOPLE}.
LanguageData.CC_Match_Child: {DEAD} is gone, but {CHILD}, a child of the marriage, lives: kin to the colony and to {PEOPLE} both, and the alliance holds through {CHILD_objective}.
